</> COMPUTER SCIENCE · SCIENTIFIC COMPUTING · SOFTWARE

Hi, I'm Jos.
I build software for hard problems.

At Los Alamos National Laboratory's T-1 group, I design original GPU algorithms for molecular simulation. I developed ALAMOS and ALAMOS-0, demonstrated 200,000 stable MD steps across 104,640 atoms without corrective Krylov iterations, and implemented Shadow XL-BOMD (Levels 0/1) with ALAMOS-0 in a native C++/MPI LAMMPS development build, now being validated for integration into open-source LAMMPS. I'm first author of our 13-author Shadow MD paper, available on arXiv and submitted to The Journal of Chemical Physics (JCP), developed with researchers at Los Alamos and Sandia National Laboratories. I'm now preparing my next first-author ALAMOS methods paper while finishing a 4.0-GPA CS degree at DePaul.

SHADOW MOLECULAR DYNAMICS

Charge conservation,
built into the algorithm.

Separate research benchmark: 104,640 atoms · NVE · 1 ps · dt 0.5 fs. The live curves and numbers above are not from that run.

How the comparison works ↗

This interactive is a self-contained teaching model, not an actual production trajectory. A neutral three-site QEq energy gives an analytical tight-charge reference. Both Shadow XL traces propagate auxiliary charge variables using the same damped recurrence, with different illustrative scalar preconditioning gains. ALAMOS-0 is a preconditioner used within Shadow XL-BOMD, not a third MD method; the toy gains do not reproduce the ALAMOS-0 implementation. The displayed residual is the magnitude of the QEq energy derivative for the selected configuration (the exact reference is zero). Changing the timestep recomputes the example at the same physical time; Reset restarts it at 0 fs. The separate 104,640-atom reference simulation used a 0.5 fs timestep and zero corrective Krylov iterations with ALAMOS-0.

ALAMOS
ORIGINAL ALGORITHMS · METHODS PAPER IN PREPARATION

ALAMOS / ALAMOS-0

I developed ALAMOS to reduce costly iterative charge updates, then advanced it to ALAMOS-0. In the tested 104,640-atom run, ALAMOS-0 sustained 200,000 steps without a corrective Krylov iteration. I am preparing a second first-author methods manuscript on ALAMOS, drawing on the measured solver and GPU performance results.
